mnemonic: What 何 for, said with a shrug rather than a raised eyebrow. She said she was coming and she is not here: なんで.
notes: なぜ is the plain why and どうして sits between the two. 何で is the casual spoken one.
sentence: 彼女は何で来ないんだろう。
sentence_meaning: I wonder why she's not coming.

mnemonic: You get shown the back 裏 of somebody and there is a knife 切 in it. His own friends, at that: うらぎる.
sentence: 彼は仲間を裏切ったの。
sentence_meaning: He betrayed his friends.

mnemonic: Fire 火 put under the thing on purpose, and whether it comes out grilled or ruined is a question of timing. Fish, right now: やく.
notes: Same reading as 役 やく, a role. This one has 火 fire in it and covers grilling, baking and burning alike.
sentence: 今、魚を焼いています。
sentence_meaning: I'm grilling fish now.

mnemonic: Something strange 怪 has happened to your own 我 body, which is a very Japanese way of putting it. Her arm, this time: けが.
notes: The characters are borrowed for sound. There is nothing to read out of 怪 strange and 我 self.
sentence: 彼女は腕を怪我した。
sentence_meaning: She injured her arm.

mnemonic: Two doors side by side with everybody funnelled between them. The school one opens at eight: もん.
notes: 入り口 いりぐち is the entrance as the way in. 門 is the gate itself, the thing standing there.
sentence: 8時に学校の門が開きます。
sentence_meaning: The gate of the school opens at eight o'clock.

mnemonic: Not 不 can 可 able 能, three characters stacked up and every one of them saying no. That report, in a day: ふかのう.
notes: 可能 かのう is possible, and 不 on the front is the usual way of turning a word round. 無理 むり is the everyday impossible, and it also covers unreasonable and overdoing it.
sentence: レポートを1日で仕上げるのは不可能です。
sentence_meaning: It's impossible to finish up the report in a day.

mnemonic: The one with the hairpin who ran the house in the old drawing, and now simply your own. My brother's is Japanese: つま.
notes: つま is your own wife when you talk about her. 奥さん おくさん is somebody else's, and what you call her to her face.
sentence: 兄の妻は日本人です。
sentence_meaning: My elder brother's wife is Japanese.

mnemonic: There are times 時 when even the patient one has had enough, and this is turning into one of them: ときには.
notes: たまに is occasionally as a rate. 時には sets up a contrast: usually not, but on occasion.
sentence: 優しい母も時には怒ります。
sentence_meaning: Even kind mothers get angry at times.

mnemonic: Speech 言 that actually gets let go of 発 instead of being thought and then swallowed. Every one of them said something: はつげん.
sentence: 会議で全員が発言した。
sentence_meaning: Everyone spoke at the conference.

mnemonic: Correct 正 and certain 確 at once, which is a step past merely right. His arithmetic does not want checking: せいかく.
notes: Same reading as 性格 せいかく, personality. This one has 正 correct in it and is about being exact.
sentence: 彼の計算は正確です。
sentence_meaning: His calculation is accurate.

mnemonic: You take the thing in 認 and can tell it from the next one 識, which is what understanding comes down to. As far as I know it is finished: にんしき.
sentence: その件は終わったと認識しています。
sentence_meaning: My understanding is that the matter is over.

mnemonic: How fast 速 by how much 度, which is a number rather than an impression. What does the Shinkansen actually do: そくど.
sentence: 新幹線の速度はどれくらいですか。
sentence_meaning: What is the speed of the Shinkansen?

mnemonic: Speech 言 that leaves you lost 迷 by the end of it. The pyramids are full of them: なぞ.
sentence: ピラミッドには謎が多いんだ。
sentence_meaning: There are a lot of mysteries about the pyramids.

mnemonic: The written mark 文 and the letter 字 learned under a roof, and the way you form them says something about you: もじ.
notes: 手紙 てがみ is a letter you post. 文字 is a letter of the alphabet, or a character.
sentence: 書いた文字には、その人の気持ちが表れる。
sentence_meaning: A person's feelings appear within their written characters.

meaning: to spew, to vomit, to holler
mnemonic: Whatever was in the mouth 口 ends up on the ground 土, and this time it was words rather than dinner: はく.
sentence: 彼は乱暴な言葉を吐いたぞ。
sentence_meaning: He spewed out some violent words.

mnemonic: An outsized head on a figure that used to be a person, and he is not far off being one: おに.
notes: 悪魔 あくま is the devil, imported. 鬼 is the Japanese ogre, the one in folk tales and in 鬼ごっこ, tag.
sentence: 彼は鬼のような人だ。
sentence_meaning: He is like a demon.

mnemonic: Something goes in sharply 刺 and everything reacts hard 激. That quiz show does it to your brain: しげき.
sentence: そのクイズ番組は脳を刺激するね。
sentence_meaning: That quiz show stimulates the brain.

mnemonic: Take the very top 最 one off the pile and there is nothing at all above it. Fastest man alive: もっとも.
notes: 一番 いちばん is the everyday most, literally number one. 最も is the formal one and sits in front of an adjective.
sentence: 彼は世界で最も早い男です。
sentence_meaning: He's the fastest man in the world.

mnemonic: Clothes 服 cut to a set of rules 制 rather than to anybody's taste. We do not have to wear one: せいふく.
sentence: 私の学校には制服がありません。
sentence_meaning: There is no uniform in my school.

mnemonic: Fire that refuses to stay where it was put 爆, let go all in one go 発. The dynamite went: ばくはつ.
sentence: ダイナマイトが爆発したんだ。
sentence_meaning: The dynamite exploded.

mnemonic: Instruction 訓 run over and over until it goes smooth 練, so that nobody has to think on the day. Fire drill, at school: くんれん.
notes: 練習 れんしゅう is practice at a skill. 訓練 is drilling, the formal and organised sort.
sentence: 学校で避難訓練がありました。
sentence_meaning: There was a fire drill at the school.

meaning: to turn around, to look back
mnemonic: The shoulders swing round 振 and the face follows 向, and she was smiling by the time it got there: ふりむく.
notes: 振り返る ふりかえる is the same movement and also does looking back on the past. 振り向く stays physical.
sentence: 彼女は振り向いて俺に微笑んだんだ。
sentence_meaning: She turned around and smiled at me.

meaning: to remove clothes, to take off
mnemonic: Something comes away from the body 月 and ends up folded over your arm. The coat, at the door: ぬぐ.
notes: 着る きる is putting clothes on. 脱ぐ is taking them off, shoes included, which matters at a Japanese front door.
sentence: コートを脱ぎます。
sentence_meaning: I will take off my coat.

mnemonic: You believe 信 them and then you lean 頼 on them, which is the two halves of it. Both ways, or it does not work: しんらい.
notes: 信用 しんよう is trusting what somebody says or does. 信頼 is trusting the person, and it is the warmer word.
sentence: お互いを信頼することが大事です。
sentence_meaning: It is important to trust each other.

meaning: to stop by, to drop by
mnemonic: You duck in under a roof 宀 on the way to somewhere else, and you are not stopping long. The bank, before school: よる.
notes: Same reading as 夜 よる, night. 寄る is a stop on the way, and 寄って is what a shopkeeper calls out at you.
sentence: 学校へ行く前に銀行に寄りました。
sentence_meaning: I stopped by the bank before going to school.

meaning: to fly, to launch in the air
mnemonic: You put the thing into the air 飛 rather than going up yourself, and the boy's paper plane is on its third lap: とばす.
notes: 飛ぶ とぶ is a thing flying. 飛ばす is you sending it up.
sentence: 子供が紙飛行機を飛ばしています。
sentence_meaning: The child is launching a paper airplane.

mnemonic: Money 貝 handed across as a stand-in 代 for whatever comes back later. He has had that book a month: かす.
notes: 借りる かりる is the other side of the same arrangement, borrowing. 貸す is you handing it out.
sentence: 私は彼に本を貸しています。
sentence_meaning: I'm lending him the book.

mnemonic: Straight off the Portuguese pão and four hundred years old in Japanese, and it is what is on the table every morning: ぱん.
notes: One of the older loanwords, from Portuguese rather than English, which is why it is not ブレッド.
sentence: 朝ご飯にはいつもパンを食べる。
sentence_meaning: I always eat bread for breakfast.

mnemonic: His help turned up at the point where you had run out of ideas, and the word is for how rare that is: ありがたい.
notes: Literally hard to exist, so rare, and ありがとう grew out of the same root.
sentence: 彼の助けは本当にありがたいな。
sentence_meaning: His help is really appreciated.

mnemonic: A figure stood over the fire 火 with the colour coming off it, and the signal ahead has just gone that way: あか.
notes: 赤い あかい is the adjective. 赤 on its own is the colour as a noun.
sentence: 信号が赤に変わりました。
sentence_meaning: The traffic light changed to red.

mnemonic: The big 大 body 体 of it done and only the edges still ragged. The report is very nearly there: だいたい.
sentence: レポートは大体終わりました。
sentence_meaning: The report is mostly finished.

mnemonic: Spines lined up, nothing sticking out, everything back where it came from. Not merely done, done properly: きちんと.
sentence: 本は本棚にきちんと返してください。
sentence_meaning: Please put the books back neatly on the bookshelf.

mnemonic: The passage behind the mouth 口 that goes first every winter, and you are in the shop asking after it: のど.
sentence: 喉にいい薬はありますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you have any good medicine for the throat?

mnemonic: Few 少 and then the mark that says do it again 々, which somehow comes out meaning less rather than more. A pinch of salt: しょうしょう.
notes: ちょっと is the everyday a little. 少々 is politer, and it is the one in 少々お待ちください.
sentence: 塩を少々入れてください。
sentence_meaning: Please put in a little salt.

mnemonic: You have 有 a name 名, which is the whole of what fame is. This stretch of coast has one and the crowds come: ゆうめい.
sentence: この海は有名で、人が大勢来ます。
sentence_meaning: This sea is famous, so many people come here.

mnemonic: The big one with a deck and people standing about on it, not the thing you row. We got on: ふね.
sentence: 私たちは船に乗った。
sentence_meaning: We got on the ship.

mnemonic: A cart wheel 車 going over and over with nobody steering it. The cat did that on the sand for ten minutes: ころがる.
notes: 転がす ころがす is you rolling something. 転がる is it rolling on its own.
sentence: 猫は砂の上で転がったんだ。
sentence_meaning: The cat rolled over on the sand.

meaning: to be able to cut, to run out, to expire
mnemonic: The line gets cut 切 without anybody cutting it and that is the end of the supply. The printer has been warning you for a week: きれる.
notes: 切る きる is you cutting something. 切れる is a thing running out, expiring or snapping by itself.
sentence: プリンターのインクが切れた。
sentence_meaning: The printer ink ran out.

mnemonic: You open the wallet expecting to be fine and there is one note sitting in it. Only that, and not a yen more: たった.
notes: Goes in front of a number, and usually with しか and a negative behind it: たった1000円しかない.
sentence: 財布の中にたった1000円しかないよ。
sentence_meaning: I only have 1,000 yen in my wallet.

mnemonic: What the talk 話 is about 題, and what everybody has decided to be about this month. That is the restaurant: わだい.
sentence: ここが話題のレストランです。
sentence_meaning: This is the restaurant that is the talk of the town.

mnemonic: Rain over the top and water the whole way through, not splashed but soaked. Caught out in it: ぬれる.
sentence: 雨で濡れてしまった。
sentence_meaning: I got wet in the rain.

meaning: on the way, while one's at it
mnemonic: You are going out anyway, so the dry cleaning can go along with you. Not a trip, an extra stop on one: ついでに.
notes: 途中 とちゅう is partway along a journey. ついでに is doing a second thing because you were going regardless.
sentence: ついでにクリーニング屋さんに寄ってきて。
sentence_meaning: Drop by the cleaners on the way.

mnemonic: Your name gets called 呼 and out 出 you come, and when it is the school ringing your parents it is never good news: よびだす.
sentence: 親が学校に呼び出されたんだ。
sentence_meaning: My parents were called in to the school.

mnemonic: Certain 確 and believing it 信, which is a step past merely expecting it. I have no doubt at all he will manage: かくしん.
sentence: 私は彼の成功を確信しています。
sentence_meaning: I am convinced of his success.

meaning: to put in, to concentrate on
mnemonic: You put something in 込 that was never in the words themselves, and the song came out different for it: こめる.
notes: 入れる いれる is putting a thing inside something. 込める is putting in what you cannot hold, feeling into a song.
sentence: 彼は感情を込めてその歌を歌ったの。
sentence_meaning: He sang that song with feeling.

mnemonic: You notice 覚 something about yourself 自, and a child young enough has simply not got there yet: じかく.
notes: 意識 いしき is consciousness, or being aware of something outside you. 自覚 is awareness of your own state or conduct.
sentence: まだ子供だから悪い事をしたという自覚がないんだ。
sentence_meaning: He has no awareness of having done a bad thing because he is still a child.

mnemonic: One seat empties and there is a hole 穴 where somebody was sitting. One free at the back: あく.
notes: Same reading as 開く あく, to open, which is the door rather than the space. The same characters read すく mean a place thinning out.
sentence: 後ろの席が空いています。
sentence_meaning: The rear seat is empty.

meaning: to be empty, to become less crowded
mnemonic: Not one seat gone but half of them, and the whole room breathes out. The restaurant at four on a Tuesday: すく.
notes: The same characters read あく mean a single spot coming free. すく is the place thinning out, and it is the すく in お腹が空く.
sentence: レストランは空いていました。
sentence_meaning: The restaurant was empty.

mnemonic: A warning spoken 警 and somebody watching closely enough to judge it 察, which between them is the job. Ring them: けいさつ.
sentence: 警察を呼んでください。
sentence_meaning: Call the police.

mnemonic: A sad 悲 sound going off 鳴 outside and every person in the room stopping at once. That was not a bird: ひめい.
sentence: 外から悲鳴が聞こえたな。
sentence_meaning: I heard a scream coming from outside.
